Derived Index Extractors and Stamps

How a replicated copy keeps its own indexes object by object: extractors (gxrextract.h) and index stamps (gxdstamp.h), DataReel 7.4.

Contents

Overview
Extractors

Overview

gxrepl never sends a set's derived indexes (derived = by_*.btx, vectors.vix): the copy keeps them itself. With derived_apply = incremental it updates each index object by object, in the same atomic batch as the data, from the objects records the writer adds to the ship log (EnableObjectNotes()). An extractor turns a record into its index entries; anything it cannot be sure of (a gap, an error, a crash, a damaged stamp) puts that folder back on a full rebuild ("rebuild needed"). Per-object apply is off by default and in 7.4 not yet for production use.

An extractor is a table of C functions (gxrExtractorOps, ABI GXR_EXTRACTOR_ABI): version, open(index_path, config, source, err, n), remove(handle, addr, bytes, len, ...) and insert(...) for each changed record (its old and new bytes), flush, count and close. It is either built into gxrepl (gxrRegisterExtractor(), as the replication example's example_records with GXREPL_EXTRA_EXTRACTORS) or loaded from a .so named by derived_extractor (the program must export DataReel's symbols to it: one copy of the library). The built-in gxvmember extractor keeps a vector index from record members (gxvmember.h).

Each index has a stamp (<index>.stamp): the log id, the record position and the entry count it is at, and the folder a derived.stamp. A copy that finds an index whose stamp does not match its position rebuilds the folder. The administrator's view: gxrepl derived status|rebuild (gxrepl).

Extractors

int gxrRegisterExtractor(const char *name, const gxrExtractorOps *ops)

Registers a built-in extractor under a name for derived_extractor.

struct gxrExtractorOps { uint32_t abi; const char *(*version)(); void *(*open)(...); int (*remove)(...); int (*insert)(...); int (*flush)(...); uint64_t (*count)(void *); void (*close)(void *); }

The functions an extractor provides; each returns 0, or -1 with a message (an error means "rebuild needed").
